Hannah / Dev — I’ve reviewed the numbers and legal redlines. Legal flagged two things: (1) the 30% cap is outside standard policy (we usually max at 25% for new customers), and (2) the uptime bump to 99.95% materially increases our exposure on high-availability regions. Legal is open if we hard-limit remedies to the Dedicated pool used by Zenora and if we add max outage triggers (e.g., >3 incidents of >15 min in a 30-day window).

Operations (Dev) — can you confirm whether we can guarantee the 120ms p95 for the two routes under a committed Dedicated pool? If not, what mitigations can we bake in (latency-tier model, cross-region failover, additional reserved capacity)?

Proposal to Execs:
- Accept 99.95% but scoped to reserved Dedicated capacity assigned to Zenora (isolation clause).
- Accept service credit cap increase to 30% only if customer signs 12-month commit and Redwood gets a 8% shadow discount during first 3 months to offset potential tail costs.
- Add a rollback clause: if latency >150ms p95 for 72 continuous hours despite mitigation, we switch to alternate model variant and cap remedy exposure to 15% for that month.

I think this is dealable; the question is approval to grant the exception and the discount. Marissa

All — after reviewing legal and ops input I approve the following one-time exception for Zenora (DEAL-8347), effective only for the pilot and subject to the conditions below: 

Approved items:
- Uptime target: 99.95% scoped to the dedicated GPU pool allocated to Zenora for the pilot.
- Service credit cap: increased to 30% monthly for pilot months, with a hard cap of $50k per month on credited amounts.
- Committed discount: 8% off list for first 3 months of the 12-month commitment; standard pricing thereafter.

Conditions / mitigations (must be in amendment):
1) Isolation: the SLA applies only to the dedicated pool named in the amendment; we will document failure domains and maintenance windows in the SOW.
2) Latency clause: we cannot commit to 120ms p95 in all production windows. We will target 120ms p95 under nominal load; operational guarantee will be p95 <=150ms. If observed p95 >150ms for 72 continuous hours despite following our mitigation playbook (redistribute load, spin additional reserved capacity, route to variant model), Redwood may apply the rollback clause and limit remedy exposure to 15% for that month.
3) Monitoring & review: nightly trace export to Zenora, and a 30/60/90 day performance review with both parties.
4) Legal approval: this exception requires countersignature from Legal (I’ve asked Legal to finalize redlines and the docusign link).

Rafael — please relay to Sanjay and Elise that we can do the pilot under these terms; include the docuSign link once Legal confirms redlines. Dev — coordinate the Dedicated pool sizing and provide an ops runbook to the customer.

Hannah
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
